payload.answer: Ok, override and land. But I need you to raise new issues: it should be agreed at the start that a post merge proof check has to be done. So that the merge check doesn't block in those cases. Then the study room does not properly displays the mermaid diagrams in the browser, it shows the mermaid code instead. I need you to also debug: why isn't plumb debug loop autonomously triggered and improves plumb workflows separately? So that when an issue is found in the outcome of plumb execution, it automatically improves itself. Then why didn't plumb identified this mermaid issue during proof checks? And once the plumb debug workflow outcome is merged, it should unlock the current session that detected the issue. Maybe that's too many different tasks to perform. There should be an available Claude session to offload some of that work to it.

options.description: I finish the merge with git -c plumb.mergeHold=false commit. It lands now; plumb-85 then shows each proof live and asks you whether you saw it working, and works through any question still open. Trade-off: main briefly holds features whose proof you haven't seen yet. Recommended because the proof hold can only clear after landing anyway.
options.label: Override and land (Recommended)

options.description: plumb-85 re-checks the 14 questions in main's checkout and asks you whatever is really open; then I override only for the proofs. Trade-off: one more round with plumb-85 (messages need your approval in its terminal) before anything lands.
options.label: Questions first, then override
